mean: uniquely blessed by nature or circumstance
lit: to receive from heaven, alone, in rich measure

use.how: Predicate or attribute about lasting natural advantages of a place or a person's gifts: 这里的条件得天独厚；得天独厚的地理位置。

near.diff: 天时地利 is favourable timing and place for one undertaking; 得天独厚 is a lasting natural advantage someone or somewhere has.

cue: A town has mild weather, rich soil and clean mountain water, so its tea is the best in the region. How do you describe its conditions?

ctx.s: 这个小镇气候温和、水源充足，种茶的条件{得天独厚}。
ctx.en: This town has a mild climate and plenty of water; its conditions for growing tea are exceptional.

ctx.s: 她有一副{得天独厚}的好嗓子，一开口就让人记住了。
ctx.en: She has a naturally gifted voice; people remember her the moment she starts singing.

ctx.s: 这座城市靠海又有深水港，发展航运可以说是{得天独厚}。
ctx.en: The city is on the coast and has a deep-water port; for shipping it is uniquely well placed.

ctx.s: “你们这儿风景这么好，游客一定很多吧？”“是啊，我们这里{得天独厚}，一年四季都有人来。”
ctx.en: "The scenery here is so lovely, you must get lots of tourists?" "Yes, we're blessed by nature here; people come all year round."

ctx.s: 别总羡慕别人{得天独厚}，没有好条件也能靠努力弥补。
ctx.en: Stop envying people who were born with every advantage; hard work can make up for what you lack.

ctx.s: 凭借{得天独厚}的地理位置，这里自古就是商旅往来的要道。
ctx.en: Thanks to its uniquely favourable location, this place has been a major trade route since ancient times.

bad.s: 他昨天买彩票中了大奖，真是{得天独厚}。
bad.en: (meant: he was really lucky to win the lottery yesterday)
bad.why: It describes lasting natural advantages of a place or a person's gifts, not a single lucky event.

bad.s: 他{得天独厚}了一个好嗓子。
bad.en: (meant: he was blessed with a good voice)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; make the voice the subject, or use the idiom as an attribute before 'voice'.

mean: so carried away by success that one forgets oneself
lit: so pleased with oneself that one forgets one's own body

story.text: Ruan Ji, one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, loved wine and played the zither well. The Book of Jin says that when he was enjoying himself he would forget his own body entirely. The phrase first described that carefree absorption; later it came to mean losing self-control out of pride after a success.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (得意忘形地) about someone who shows off or gets careless after a success; often in warnings: 别得意忘形。

near.diff: 忘乎所以 can come from any excitement; 得意忘形 comes specifically from success and self-satisfaction.

cue: Your friend just got promoted and is already bragging and ordering old colleagues around. What warning do you give?

ctx.s: 他考了第一名就{得意忘形}，在班上到处炫耀。
ctx.en: As soon as he came top of the class he got carried away and showed off to everyone.

ctx.s: 刚升职别{得意忘形}，大家都在看着你呢。
ctx.en: You've only just been promoted, don't let it go to your head; everyone is watching you.

ctx.s: 比赛领先了几分，球员们有点{得意忘形}，结果被对手反超了。
ctx.en: A few points ahead, the players got cocky, and the other team overtook them.

ctx.s: “我中奖了！”“恭喜，不过别{得意忘形}，先想想钱该怎么用。”
ctx.en: "I won the prize!" "Congratulations, but don't get carried away; think first about how to use the money."

ctx.s: 人在顺境中最容易{得意忘形}，这时候更要保持清醒。
ctx.en: People lose their heads most easily when things are going well; that's when you most need to stay clear-headed.

ctx.s: 他刚签下一笔大单，一时{得意忘形}，在酒桌上把公司的计划全说了出去。
ctx.en: Having just landed a big deal, he got carried away and blurted out the company's whole plan over drinks.

bad.s: 看到孩子平安回家，妈妈{得意忘形}地哭了。
bad.en: (meant: seeing her child home safe, the mother wept with joy)
bad.why: It criticises conceit after a success; relief and tears of joy have nothing to do with it.

bad.s: 老师表扬了我，我感到很{得意忘形}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher praised me and I felt very proud and happy)
bad.why: It is a judgement on someone's behaviour, not a pleasant feeling one reports, so it cannot follow 'I feel very'.

mean: to muddle along, doing only what gets one by
lit: if one can get by, just get by for now

story.text: On Mount Wutai lived a bird called the hanhao chong. In midsummer its feathers were bright and it sang, 'Even the phoenix is not as fine as me.' By the depth of winter its feathers had fallen out, it looked like a bare chick, and all it sang was, 'Get by if I can, just get by.'
story.source: 元·陶宗仪《南村辍耕录·寒号虫》

use.how: Predicate or attribute (得过且过的心态) about a person's attitude to work or life: no aims, no effort beyond getting through the day.

near.diff: 敷衍了事 is doing one task carelessly to be done with it; 得过且过 is a general attitude of living without aims.

cue: Your cousin has no plans, does the minimum at work and says he'll think about the future later. How do you describe the way he lives?

ctx.s: 他对工作没什么追求，每天{得过且过}。
ctx.en: He has no ambitions at work; he just muddles through each day.

ctx.s: 年轻人不能{得过且过}，总得为将来打算打算。
ctx.en: Young people can't just drift along; they have to plan for the future.

ctx.s: 这家工厂的管理人员{得过且过}，设备坏了也没人愿意修。
ctx.en: The managers at this factory just get by; when equipment breaks, nobody wants to fix it.

ctx.s: 你难道就打算这样{得过且过}下去吗？
ctx.en: Are you really planning to keep drifting along like this?

ctx.s: 失业以后，他整天{得过且过}，连简历都懒得改。
ctx.en: After losing his job he just let the days drift by and couldn't even be bothered to update his CV.

ctx.s: 抱着{得过且过}的心态，是做不好任何事情的。
ctx.en: With a just-get-by attitude, you won't do anything well.

bad.s: 这次考试我{得过且过}，终于通过了。
bad.en: (meant: I scraped through this exam)
bad.why: The 'get by' here is not passing an exam; the idiom criticises an aimless attitude to life, not a narrow pass.

bad.s: 爷爷生活很节俭，日子{得过且过}，从不浪费。
bad.en: (meant: grandpa lives frugally and never wastes anything)
bad.why: It means lacking effort or aims, not being thrifty; it would insult the grandfather.

mean: the way the general trend is heading
lit: where the great momentum is heading

use.how: Usually after 是, or as the object of 面对 or 顺应, about broad social, economic or historical trends: 这是大势所趋。

near.diff: 势在必行 says something must be done now; 大势所趋 says the general trend is heading that way.

cue: A bookshop owner asks whether selling online is a passing fad. You say the whole industry is moving there and resisting is pointless. What do you call it?

ctx.s: 用手机付款已经是{大势所趋}，很多小店也不收现金了。
ctx.en: Paying by phone is now the way things are going; many small shops no longer take cash.

ctx.s: 新能源汽车取代燃油车，是{大势所趋}。
ctx.en: New-energy cars replacing petrol cars is the direction things are clearly heading.

ctx.s: “我们公司还要不要做线上业务？”“必须做，这是{大势所趋}。”
ctx.en: "Should our company still go into online business?" "We have to; that's where everything is heading."

ctx.s: 面对{大势所趋}，传统书店只能想办法转型。
ctx.en: Faced with the general trend, traditional bookshops can only try to reinvent themselves.

ctx.s: 人口向大城市集中，既是{大势所趋}，也带来了不少问题。
ctx.en: People concentrating in big cities is an unstoppable trend, but it also brings many problems.

ctx.s: 难道你看不出远程办公是{大势所趋}吗？
ctx.en: Can't you see that remote work is where things are heading?

bad.s: 看天色，今天下午{大势所趋}会下雨。
bad.en: (meant: from the look of the sky it will probably rain this afternoon)
bad.why: It is about broad social or historical trends, not a forecast of a single event like the weather.

bad.s: 我{大势所趋}地换了一份新工作。
bad.en: (meant: I followed the trend and changed jobs)
bad.why: It is not an adverb describing a person's action; it names a broad trend and usually follows 'is'.

mean: to step forward boldly to face a challenge
lit: to straighten one's body and step out

use.how: Predicate about someone who steps forward when others hang back, to face danger or trouble on others' behalf: 关键时刻，他挺身而出。

near.diff: 见义勇为 is praise for bravely helping a stranger, often against a criminal; 挺身而出 stresses stepping forward in any crisis when others hold back.

cue: A man collapses on a crowded train and everyone freezes, until one woman pushes through and starts first aid. What did she do?

ctx.s: 看到同事被老板冤枉，他马上{挺身而出}替她说话。
ctx.en: When he saw his colleague wrongly blamed by the boss, he stepped up at once and spoke for her.

ctx.s: 公司遇到危机时，是她{挺身而出}，带大家渡过了难关。
ctx.en: When the company was in crisis, it was she who stepped up and led everyone through it.

ctx.s: 地铁上有人突然晕倒，一位护士{挺身而出}，给他做了急救。
ctx.en: Someone fainted on the subway, and a nurse stepped forward and gave him first aid.

ctx.s: “这件事就没人敢管吗？”“总得有人{挺身而出}吧。”
ctx.en: "Doesn't anyone dare deal with this?" "Somebody has to step up."

ctx.s: 关键时刻能{挺身而出}的人，才值得大家信任。
ctx.en: Only people who step forward when it really matters deserve everyone's trust.

ctx.s: 那年洪水来袭，村里的年轻人纷纷{挺身而出}，日夜守在堤坝上。
ctx.en: The year the flood came, the village's young people stepped forward one after another and guarded the dykes day and night.

bad.s: 老师走进教室时，全班同学{挺身而出}向他问好。
bad.en: (meant: when the teacher came in, the whole class stood up to greet him)
bad.why: It means bravely stepping forward to face danger or trouble, not physically standing up from one's seat.

bad.s: 小王总喜欢{挺身而出}，抢着回答老师的每个问题。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang is always eager to answer every question)
bad.why: It is about facing danger or difficulty for others, not eagerness to speak up in class.

mean: the whole room bursts out laughing
lit: the whole hall roars with great laughter

use.how: Predicate whose subject is a group in one room (全班、观众、大家), or object of 引起/引得: 引得全场哄堂大笑。

near.diff: 捧腹大笑 is one or more people laughing very hard; 哄堂大笑 is a whole room bursting into laughter at once.

cue: In the middle of a quiet lecture a puppy trots onto the stage, and every student in the hall laughs at the same moment. What happens?

ctx.s: 他的一句玩笑，引得全班{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: One joke from him and the whole class burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 主持人不小心念错了名字，台下观众{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: The host misread a name by accident and the whole audience roared with laughter.

ctx.s: 小明把“老师”写成了“老鼠”，同学们看了{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: Xiao Ming wrote 'mouse' instead of 'teacher', and the whole class burst out laughing when they saw it.

ctx.s: 婚礼上，新郎紧张得把誓词念反了，宾客们{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: At the wedding the groom was so nervous he read his vows backwards, and the guests all burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 你知道他在年会上说了什么，竟然让全场{哄堂大笑}吗？
ctx.en: Do you know what he said at the annual party that made the whole room crack up?

ctx.s: 一只小狗突然跑上讲台，教室里响起一阵{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: A puppy suddenly ran up onto the platform and the classroom erupted in laughter.

bad.s: 他一个人在房间里看喜剧，{哄堂大笑}。
bad.en: (meant: alone in his room watching a comedy, he laughed out loud)
bad.why: It needs a whole roomful of people laughing together; one person laughing alone cannot be described this way.

bad.s: 我们在公园里{哄堂大笑}地玩了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: we played and laughed happily in the park all afternoon)
bad.why: It is one sudden burst of laughter from a room of people, not a long stretch of fun, and it is not an adverb.

mean: nervously apprehensive about what is coming
lit: heart up, heart down: not at ease

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (忐忑不安地) about one's own nervous state while waiting for an uncertain outcome: 等结果时我心里忐忑不安。

near.diff: 毛骨悚然 is the creepy horror at an eerie sight or story; 忐忑不安 is nervous worry about how something will turn out.
提心吊胆 is lasting fear that something bad or dangerous will happen; 忐忑不安 is restless unease over how an uncertain matter will turn out.

cue: You've handed in your resignation letter and now spend the whole night wondering how your boss will react. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 听说老板要找我谈话，我心里{忐忑不安}，不知道是好事还是坏事。
ctx.en: Hearing the boss wanted a word with me, I felt uneasy, not knowing whether it was good news or bad.

ctx.s: 第一次见女朋友的父母，他心里{忐忑不安}。
ctx.en: Meeting his girlfriend's parents for the first time, he felt very nervous inside.

ctx.s: 她{忐忑不安}地推开了面试官办公室的门。
ctx.en: Full of nerves, she pushed open the door of the interviewer's office.

ctx.s: “医生，检查结果怎么样？”妈妈{忐忑不安}地问。
ctx.en: "Doctor, how are the test results?" Mum asked anxiously.

ctx.s: 交了辞职信以后，他整晚{忐忑不安}，不知道老板会怎么回应。
ctx.en: After handing in his resignation he was uneasy all night, not knowing how his boss would respond.

ctx.s: 带着{忐忑不安}的心情，他拨通了那个多年没联系的号码。
ctx.en: With his heart in his mouth, he dialled the number he hadn't called in years.

bad.s: 这部恐怖片太可怕了，我看得{忐忑不安}。
bad.en: (meant: the horror film was so scary I was terrified)
bad.why: It is nervous worry about an uncertain outcome, not horror at something creepy on screen.

bad.s: 他的消息{忐忑不安}了我一整天。
bad.en: (meant: his news made me anxious all day)
bad.why: It describes the subject's own state and cannot take an object; it needs 'made me' in front of it.

mean: creepy enough to make one's hair stand on end
lit: hair and bones stand up in fright

use.how: Predicate, often in 令人毛骨悚然 or 听得毛骨悚然, about eerie sights, sounds, stories or gruesome details.

near.diff: 不寒而栗 is more formal and often about the thought of danger or cruelty; 毛骨悚然 is the physical creep at an eerie sight, sound or story.

cue: Alone at home after midnight, you hear slow footsteps in the empty flat upstairs. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 半夜听到楼上传来哭声，我不禁{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: Hearing crying from upstairs in the middle of the night made my hair stand on end.

ctx.s: 这个鬼故事讲得太真了，听得大家{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: The ghost story was told so vividly that it gave everyone the creeps.

ctx.s: 那条小路又黑又静，走在上面让人{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: That little path is dark and silent; walking along it sends shivers down your spine.

ctx.s: “你看过那部恐怖片吗？”“看过，有几个镜头现在想起来还{毛骨悚然}。”
ctx.en: "Have you seen that horror film?" "Yes, a few of the scenes still give me the creeps when I think of them."

ctx.s: 警方公布的案情细节令人{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: The details of the case released by the police are chilling.

ctx.s: 他回头一看，镜子里竟多了一张脸，顿时{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: He looked back and saw an extra face in the mirror, and his hair stood on end.

bad.s: 明天就要面试了，我紧张得{毛骨悚然}。
bad.en: (meant: I have an interview tomorrow and I'm extremely nervous)
bad.why: It is horror at something eerie or gruesome, not nerves before an upcoming event.

bad.s: 今天太冷了，我冻得{毛骨悚然}。
bad.en: (meant: it's so cold I've got goosebumps)
bad.why: It describes fear at something creepy, not a physical reaction to cold.

lit: startling the heart and shaking the soul

story.text: In his Grading of Poets, the critic Zhong Rong praised the anonymous 'Old Poems' of the Han: their words were gentle and beautiful, their meaning sad and far-reaching; they startled the heart and shook the soul, and were worth almost a thousand gold pieces a word. The phrase first praised deeply moving writing; today it describes thrilling or dangerous events.

use.how: Predicate or attribute about events, scenes, matches or experiences full of tension and danger: 比赛打得惊心动魄；惊心动魄的一夜。

near.diff: 扣人心弦 is gripping suspense in a story or match; 惊心动魄 adds danger and shock, as in a near-disaster.

cue: The final went to the last second, with the lead changing hands again and again and the crowd on its feet. How was the match?

ctx.s: 这场决赛打得{惊心动魄}，直到最后一秒才分出胜负。
ctx.en: The final was a nail-biter; it wasn't decided until the last second.

ctx.s: 电影里的追车场面拍得{惊心动魄}。
ctx.en: The car-chase scenes in the film are heart-stopping.

ctx.s: “昨晚的比赛你看了吗？”“看了，太{惊心动魄}了，我的心都快跳出来了。”
ctx.en: "Did you watch last night's match?" "Yes, it was so thrilling my heart nearly jumped out of my chest."

ctx.s: 飞机遇到强气流的那几分钟，真是{惊心动魄}。
ctx.en: Those few minutes when the plane hit severe turbulence were truly terrifying.

ctx.s: 回忆起那次雪山遇险，他说那是一生中最{惊心动魄}的一夜。
ctx.en: Recalling his ordeal on the snowy mountain, he said it was the most harrowing night of his life.

ctx.s: 这本小说描写了一场{惊心动魄}的海上救援。
ctx.en: The novel describes a breathtaking rescue at sea.

bad.s: 听说考试推迟了，我{惊心动魄}。
bad.en: (meant: I was shocked to hear the exam had been postponed)
bad.why: It describes thrilling or dangerous events and scenes, not a person's surprise at a piece of news.

bad.s: 这个公园的风景{惊心动魄}，很适合散步。
bad.en: (meant: the park's scenery is breathtakingly beautiful and great for walks)
bad.why: English 'breathtaking' misleads: it means tension and danger, not beauty; so a calm park cannot be described this way.

mean: refreshingly new to see or hear
lit: ears and eyes made new all at once

use.how: Mostly in 令人/让人耳目一新 or 耳目一新的感觉, about the fresh impression a design, work, style or change makes on its audience.

near.diff: 焕然一新 says the thing itself now looks brand new; 耳目一新 says the viewer or listener gets a fresh, new impression.

cue: A band turns a tired old folk song into a jazz piece, and the audience feels they are hearing it for the first time. What effect does it have?

ctx.s: 餐厅重新装修后，让人{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: After the restaurant was redecorated, it felt completely fresh.

ctx.s: 这位新导演的作品给人一种{耳目一新}的感觉。
ctx.en: This new director's work feels refreshingly original.

ctx.s: “这次的设计方案怎么样？”“很有创意，看了让人{耳目一新}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think of the design proposal?" "Very creative; it's a breath of fresh air."

ctx.s: 新校长推出的几项改革，令老师们{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: The reforms introduced by the new head struck the teachers as refreshingly new.

ctx.s: 乐队把老歌改编成了爵士风格，听起来{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: The band rearranged the old song in a jazz style, and it sounds completely fresh.

ctx.s: 换了新的排版以后，这本杂志是不是让你{耳目一新}？
ctx.en: Since the magazine changed its layout, doesn't it feel refreshingly new to you?

bad.s: 我昨天买了一部{耳目一新}的手机。
bad.en: (meant: I bought a brand-new phone yesterday)
bad.why: It describes the fresh impression something makes on people, not that an object is newly bought.

bad.s: 他{耳目一新}地看着窗外的风景。
bad.en: (meant: he looked at the view with fresh eyes)
bad.why: It is not an adverb for how someone looks; it is the effect something has on its audience.
